chapters.title: The Addresses Beneath the Lamp
chapters.description: Old Eda brings a bundle of addresses, each struck through in red. The King remembers their occupants as children. Council inspectors call them condemned properties, yet rent is collected every Friday.

choices.label: Verify the rent ledgers with Eda
choices.success: The first promise was not made to a monarch at all. It was made to families displaced by the new roof. You preserve the evidence for the tenant committee, which changes whose testimony the Council must answer.
choices.failure: Your effort is noticed before you can finish. A witness hides the evidence for you until you return.

choices.label: Speak to the tenants without revealing the royal seal

choices.failure: The witness refuses for now. You learn who must be protected before they will speak.

chapters.title: A New Oath in the Lamplight
chapters.description: At Lantern Court the King, tenants, lamp-lighters and Council witnesses meet. The evidence now demands an enforceable answer. The King's crown can be broken, or surrendered to a shared trust.

choices.label: Dissolve the crown and make a public trust
choices.success: The royal seal breaks under a hundred hands. The streets receive their lamps by right, funded by a transparent levy. Eda keeps the first independent register; the King is free of his debt.
choices.failure: The Council blocks the motion. Return with another witness or find a more modest covenant.

choices.label: Bind the King to a limited covenant
choices.success: The King gives up the right to feed on stolen light. Wardens and households hold the key to his crown. Lanterns return slowly, but their keepers have names again.
choices.failure: The King hears only another promise to be forgotten. You will need stronger witnesses to secure his assent.

choices.label: Use the language of the archives to preserve every signature
choices.success: Your careful record gives the court no room to erase the families a second time. The trust is signed publicly and the crown becomes a museum piece.
choices.failure: The court questions your authority. The evidence survives, but the final decree waits.
